blueprint.executiveSummary: Paraag Marathe & John Lynch enter November 2026 with $35.16M in gross 2026 cap space ($28.66M effective after in-season injury reserve buffer). Rather than spending to zero in-season, SF's multi-year model relies on rolling $22M–$28M of unused 2026 cap space into 2027 to offset rising Year-2/Year-3 option proration on Brock Purdy, Nick Bosa, Fred Warner, and Trent Williams.

strategicPillars.title: 1. Rollover Cap Preservation ($25M+ Target)
strategicPillars.detail: Unused 2026 cap space carries over 1-for-1 into 2027 under Article 13 of the NFL CBA. Keeping ~$25M untouched turns a tight 2027 cap sheet into comfortable operating headroom without forcing premature restructures on aging veterans.

strategicPillars.title: 2. Option-Bonus & Void-Year Architecture
strategicPillars.detail: SF structures core stars (Purdy $7.55M option proration, Bosa $8.85M option proration) with low P5 base salaries and spring option exercises that trigger April 1st—maximizing trade flexibility prior to bonus exercise dates.

strategicPillars.title: 3. Rookie-Scale Trench Pipeline (2025–2026 Classes)
strategicPillars.detail: Drafting 19 combined players across 2025–2026—heavily weighted toward DL/OL (Mykel Williams, Alfred Collins, Gracen Halton, Romello Height, Carver Willis)—insulates the cap from middle-class free-agent inflation.
